skill.name: code-instructor
skill.description: Educational coding skill that teaches programming concepts while building working applications. It explains code step by step, adapts to learner skill level, highlights common mistakes, and can use a bundled annotator script to create teaching-focused comments.
skill.summary: Teach programming through guided, incremental app development.
skill.author: Emz1998

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, resource paths, and educational examples. The confirmed risks are the local annotator script write path and the documented command that runs it on a user-supplied file. No evidence found for prompt injection, credential access, data exfiltration, or malicious network behavior.

remediation.issue: The annotator script writes an output path derived from the input filename.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit output path or refuse overwrites before writing annotated files.

remediation.issue: The skill documents a shell command that runs a bundled script on user-provided files.
remediation.suggestion: State that the command should run only after user approval and only on intended local source files.

remediation.issue: Educational Markdown code fences are repeatedly flagged as executable patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Label examples clearly as non-executable when they are only explanatory snippets.

content.value_statement: Learning code is harder when examples feel disconnected from real work. This skill teaches concepts while building working apps step by step.
actual_capabilities: Breaks application builds into small teaching phases.
Explains purpose, prerequisites, execution flow, and common mistakes.
Adapts explanation depth for beginner, intermediate, and advanced learners.
Uses bundled references for teaching patterns and common mistakes.
Provides a Python annotator script that inserts teaching comment markers.
limitations: The annotator script writes local files and requires careful path selection.
The strongest guidance covers Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, and React.
Generated applications still need normal testing and production review.
Lessons can be verbose when a user wants only concise code.

use_cases.title: Build a First App
use_cases.description: Create a small working app while learning each concept in sequence.

use_cases.title: Understand Existing Code
use_cases.description: Turn unfamiliar code into a guided lesson with comments and execution flow.

use_cases.title: Prepare Coding Lessons
use_cases.description: Structure examples, corrections, and common mistake explanations for learners.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Beginner Project
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants to learn through a small app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Teach me by building a simple todo app. Explain each file, each major line, and why each step matters.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Code Block
prompt_templates.scenario: A learner has code they do not understand.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this code like a lesson. Cover the purpose, prerequisites, execution flow, common mistakes, and a small practice change.

prompt_templates.title: Debug as a Lesson
prompt_templates.scenario: A learner has an error and needs the concept behind the fix.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me debug this error. Show what went wrong, why it happened, the fix, and the general rule I should remember.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Advanced Build
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced learner wants architecture and trade-off guidance.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build this feature in phases from simple to production-minded. Explain trade-offs, testing points, architecture choices, and refactoring moments.

output_examples.input: I want to build a todo app and learn React state.
output_examples.output: The skill creates a phased lesson plan that starts with static items, then adds state, forms, completion, deletion, and storage.

output_examples.input: Why is my async JavaScript returning undefined?
output_examples.output: The response explains timing, shows why the value is read too early, and introduces safer async handling.

output_examples.input: Make this file easier for students to study.
output_examples.output: The skill can suggest annotating the file with purpose notes, parameter notes, return notes, loop notes, and condition notes.

best_practices: Share the learner skill level before requesting a lesson.
Build the smallest working version before adding polish.
Review each major step before moving to the next concept.
anti_patterns: Do not request a large app without learning checkpoints.
Do not run the annotator script on files you do not intend to annotate.
Do not skip the reason behind a fix when the goal is learning.

faq.question: Can this skill write complete applications?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to build apps incrementally while explaining each important decision.

faq.question: Is it only for beginners?
faq.answer: No. It can adjust from syntax-level explanations to architecture and trade-off discussions.

faq.question: Which languages does it emphasize?
faq.answer: The references emphasize Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, and React teaching patterns.

faq.question: Does the script change my original file?
faq.answer: The script reads the original file and writes a separate annotated file path derived from the name.

faq.question: Can it help with debugging?
faq.answer: Yes. It frames errors as lessons by explaining the cause, fix, and reusable rule.

faq.question: What security caution should users know?
faq.answer: The optional annotator script reads and writes local files, so users should choose paths carefully.
